title: Power Rankings: Bulls, Cats make moves
heading: 2004-05 Power Rankings: Week 21

rankings.summaryHtml: Suns play 10 of their final 13 games at home. Of course, as good as they are on the road -- leading the league at 29-8 -- maybe that closing sked helps San Antonio more than Phoenix.
rankings.summaryText: Suns play 10 of their final 13 games at home. Of course, as good as they are on the road -- leading the league at 29-8 -- maybe that closing sked helps San Antonio more than Phoenix.

rankings.summaryHtml: Sorry. Don't care how impressive Heat looked winning at Suns' pace. Lose to Charlotte the next night and you forfeit No. 1.

rankings.summaryHtml: Pop thinks Duncan will make an appearance during the final five games of the regular season. Dare we say, even without TD until the playoffs, Spurs will hang on to a top-two seed.

rankings.summaryHtml: As hot as Nuggets are, look at Sonics' division lead. It's still nearly 10 games, in spite of stubborn Seattle's recent turmoil.

rankings.summaryHtml: All Rockets needed to finally seize No. 5 out West was a win over Duncan-less Spurs. Instead Houston joined Atlanta and Charlotte as the only teams to lose to SA with Duncan out.

rankings.summaryHtml: Why is a Lakers comparison so apt for these switch-flippers? One Detroit observer we trust says the champs' problem is arrogance against lesser teams. Just like the old Lakers.

rankings.summaryHtml: Winner of the Dallas-Sacto season series has lost the teams' last three playoff matchups. So maybe Mavs (3-1 this season) would prefer seeing Houston in Round 1.

rankings.summaryHtml: The committee didn't believe it when some of our Nuggets pals said they were gunning for the seventh seed out West. But take a look: Denver is much closer to No. 7 than No. 9.

rankings.summaryHtml: Winning five in a row at this point -- three on the road -- is as impressive as anything these Bulls have achieved. So it's almost time, for the first time since '98, to print up playoff tickets.

rankings.summaryHtml: This might be an omen. The same week word leaks out that Celts want to add some black to their unis next season, they drop three straight and anger their coach with their cockiness.

rankings.summaryHtml: Looks like they got the right Jordan this time. Eddie likely won't win Coach of the Year, but he has Wiz off to a 2-2 start on a crucial five-game trip ... without the injured Jamison.

rankings.summaryHtml: Our money's on Philly for the big Monday night showdown. Can't see Webber losing both games to his old team.

rankings.summaryHtml: The club record for road wins in a season is 19. But after crashing at home to Hornets, it'll be tough for Grizz to win three more roadies, given their rough remaining schedule.

rankings.summaryHtml: How good a coaching job has Carlisle done? Consider that Pacers' projected starting lineup of Tinsley, Miller, Artest, Foster and O'Neal has combined to play zero games together.

rankings.summaryHtml: The good news? Wolves apparently haven't quit. The bad news? They probably waited too long to find a groove.

rankings.summaryHtml: Why all the gloom and doom? Philly's on a 6-2 surge, with a 3½-game lead on the only team that can really catch up (Nets).

rankings.summaryHtml: Cavs haven't won a road game, for any coach, since Jan. 22. And none of the 10 teams they've beaten on the road -- not one -- has had a winning record when the game was played.

rankings.summaryHtml: Whether or not Nets claim that No. 8 spot, they have to be somewhat encouraged by their 19-17 record since losing Jefferson. Jersey easily could have folded instead.

rankings.summaryHtml: A letter writer to the LA Times says Kobe didn't choose Lakers over Clips; he turned Lakers into Clips. The standings back  up the claim: Clips are only a half-game behind their neighbors.

rankings.summaryHtml: It's one thing if you fire a coach in March and you have Brendan Malone to take over. It's another when Johnny Davis, like him or not, is replaced by someone with no experience.

rankings.summaryHtml: Lakers went 6-8 in the 14 games Kobe missed. So you can't suggest that was the stretch that doomed L.A.'s playoff bid, because its 14 games this month have been uglier (4-10).
